entries.04270caa7626e9e6: This business involves insurance underwriting and asset management by overseas insurers (overseas subsidiaries and affiliates) in various countries, and by the overseas divisions and overseas branches of the company and its domestic non-life insurance subsidiaries in Japan and at overseas bases. In the United States, it is expanding underwriting through local contracts via subsidiaries and targeting the growing US MGA market through MS Transverse (an MGA is an agent entrusted with authority by insurers and broadly handling underwriting and loss adjustment as well as sales), and it has also invested in W.R.Berkley Corporation, a leading US specialty insurance company. In its Lloyd's reinsurance business, it curbed underwriting of natural disaster risks while selectively expanding underwriting of other risks. In Asia, it is developing the retail market using digital technology in partnership with platform companies. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,462,744 million (prior year: ¥2,124,151 million), the largest of the seven categories. Insurance revenue from policyholders located in the United States was ¥940,980 million (prior year: ¥708,006 million). Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥234,456 million (prior year: ¥177,397 million). The company explains that it earned profit well above the prior year, reflecting expansion of US business, fewer natural disasters and the effect of the sale of shares in Challenger Limited, an Australian financial group. Equity-method affiliates include BOCOM MSIG Life Insurance Company Limited (voting rights held: 37.5%) and Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited (40.0%). Number of employees at overseas insurance subsidiaries was 10,297 (as of March 31, 2026).
entries.058fe4ec2147c5cb: This business is one in which Mitsui Direct General Insurance Company, Limited, specializing in internet-based automobile insurance, underwrites non-life insurance and manages assets in Japan. It is a subsidiary in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights and has a management agreement with the company. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥40,265 million (prior year: ¥35,924 million), the sixth largest of the seven categories. Revenue increased as new contracts grew, but the loss ratio rose, and profit attributable to owners of the parent was a loss for the year of ¥2,248 million (prior year: loss for the year of ¥1,479 million). Number of employees was 514 (as of March 31, 2026).
entries.12df43b0aedbfb04: This business is one in which Mitsui Sumitomo Primary Life Insurance Company, Limited underwrites life insurance and manages assets in Japan. It is a subsidiary in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights, and it is advancing the provision of life insurance products and services that support asset building, extension of asset longevity and smooth asset succession, such as inheritance and gifts, in response to growing interest in these areas. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥106,741 million (prior year: ¥108,018 million), the fifth largest of the seven categories. Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥127,359 million (prior year: ¥50,996 million). The reasons cited include an increase in interest income and the effects of interest rate and currency fluctuations. Number of employees was 418 (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.1f0bcc9c3a859921: This business is one in which Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Company, Limited underwrites non-life insurance and manages assets in Japan. It is a subsidiary in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights and has a management agreement with the company. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,888,116 million (prior year: ¥1,800,017 million), the second largest of the seven categories after overseas business. Revenue increased in automobile insurance and fire insurance. Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥182,987 million (prior year: ¥108,601 million). The reasons cited include a decrease in insurance claims incurred due to domestic natural disasters. Number of employees was 12,731 (as of March 31, 2026), the largest among the group's companies. Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance and Aioi Nissay Dowa Insurance have reached final agreement to merge with April 1, 2027 as the effective date, and have concluded a merger agreement (this is planned and had not been realized as of submission on June 30, 2026).

entries.6b874a49a48bff48: This business is one in which Mitsui Sumitomo Aioi Life Insurance Company, Limited underwrites life insurance and manages assets in Japan. It is a subsidiary in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights. It mainly offers protection-type products and has expanded the menu of its healthcare service 'ＭＳＡ Care', which helps with early detection of illnesses. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥256,278 million (prior year: ¥252,543 million), the fourth largest of the seven categories. Profit attributable to owners of the parent was a loss for the year of ¥60,293 million (prior year: profit for the year of ¥22,280 million). Insurance revenue rose, reflecting an increase in the provision of protection services, but the company explains that the recording of losses on bond sales weighed on results. Number of employees was 2,486 (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.74fb0ebb2f20f2d2: This business is one in which Aioi Nissay Dowa Insurance Company, Limited underwrites non-life insurance and manages assets in Japan. It is a subsidiary in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights and has a management agreement with the company. Insurance revenue from external customers (insurance revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,383,727 million (prior year: ¥1,329,133 million), the third largest of the seven categories. Revenue increased in automobile insurance and fire insurance. Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥118,983 million (prior year: ¥67,632 million). The reasons cited include a decrease in insurance claims incurred due to natural disasters in Japan and overseas. Number of employees was 12,515 (as of March 31, 2026), the second largest after Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance. It has concluded a merger agreement with Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance with April 1, 2027 as the effective date (this is planned and had not been realized as of submission on June 30, 2026).

entries.c99bfd05bf39947c: These are business segments not included in reportable segments, and business activities that generate other revenue. Specifically, these include the domestic non-life insurance business conducted by domestic insurers outside reportable segments, the financial services business and digital risk-related services business conducted by group companies other than domestic insurers, and the company's business investments in companies outside the group. The financial services business is carried on by domestic non-life insurance subsidiaries, Mitsui Sumitomo DS Asset Management Company, Limited and others, in asset management, financial guarantee, defined contribution pension, ART (Alternative Risk Transfer), individual lending-related and venture capital businesses. Mitsui Sumitomo DS Asset Management is an equity-method affiliate, with voting rights held of 15.0%, but it is treated as an affiliate because it has substantial influence. The digital risk-related services business comprises risk management and other businesses conducted by MS&AD InterRisk Research & Consulting, Inc., in which the company holds 100.0% of the voting rights, and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥19,156 million (prior year: ¥19,725 million), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥15,253 million (prior year: ¥13,608 million). Number of employees was 7,417 (as of March 31, 2026), being the number of employees in the risk-related services business and others conducted by group companies other than domestic insurance companies.
